result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic dev [application-arguments...] [options]

Run the application with development watchers.

Arguments:
  application-arguments  Arguments after -- are passed to the application.

Options:
  --no-restore             Skip the .NET restore and the JavaScript package install. The build does
                           not install missing frontend packages either.
  --no-frontend-watch      Build the frontend once instead of starting its development server or
                           watcher.
  --no-dotnet-watch        Run the application once instead of restarting it under dotnet watch
                           after C# edits.
  --dry-run                Print the evaluated project configuration and exit without changing files
                           or starting processes.
  --no-build               Skip the .NET restore and build before the Window starts, as dotnet run
                           --no-build does. dotnet watch still builds after C# edits.
  --environment, -e <NAME=VALUE...>
                           Set an environment variable for the Window process, as dotnet run -e
                           does. Repeat it for several variables.
  --project, -p <project>  The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                           current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                           The build configuration. [default: Debug]
  --launch-profile <NAME>  Run the Window with this profile from Properties/launchSettings.json. By
                           default dev uses no launch profile.
  --verbosity, -v <LEVEL>  The MSBuild verbosity of the builds the command runs: q[uiet], m[inimal],
                           n[ormal], d[etailed] or diag[nostic]. Without it, each command uses its
                           own default. [choices: q, quiet, m, minimal, n, normal, d, detailed,
                           diag, diagnostic]
  -h, --help               Show help
  --version                Show version
  --format <human|json>    Select o
[truncated]

result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic doctor [options]

Check the project and development environment.

Options:
  --aot                       With --runtime, check a publish with -p:PublishAot=true.
                              [conflicts: no-aot]
  --no-aot                    With --runtime, check a publish with -p:PublishAot=false.
                              [conflicts: aot]
  --self-contained            With --runtime, check a publish with --self-contained true.
                              [conflicts: no-self-contained]
  --no-self-contained         With --runtime, check a publish with --self-contained false.
                              [conflicts: self-contained]
  --project, -p <project>     The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                              current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                              The build configuration to evaluate. Defaults to Debug, or Release
                              with --runtime as dotnet publish does.
  --fail-on <fail-on>         Fail when a check reaches this status: never, fail or warn. Defaults
                              to fail in both output modes.
  --runtime, --rid, -r <rid>  Also check deployment prerequisites for this runtime identifier, for
                              example linux-x64, win-x64 or osx-arm64.
  -h, --help                  Show help
  --version                   Show version
  --format <human|json>       Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic doctor --project ./MyApp.csproj
  dotnet runic doctor --runtime linux-x64 --aot
  dotnet runic doctor --format json

Usage: dotnet runic package [options]

Package the application for distribution: MSIX, .app and disk image, Flatpak, AppImage, deb, rpm or
a Flathub manifest.

Commands:
  appimage  Package the application as an AppImage that uses the host's GTK and WebKitGTK. Runs on
            Linux with appimagetool.
  deb       Package the application as a Debian package. Runs on Linux with dpkg-deb.
  flathub   Write a Flathub source-build manifest with offline NuGet and npm sources from the
            committed lock files. --build builds it with flatpak-builder on Linux.
  flatpak   Package the application as a Flatpak bundle on the GNOME runtime. Runs on Linux with
            flatpak-builder.
  macos     Package the application as an .app bundle in a disk image, and with --pkg an installer
            package. Runs on macOS.
  rpm       Package the application as an rpm. Runs on Linux with rpmbuild, also on Debian and
            Ubuntu.
  windows   Package the application as an MSIX package. Runs on Windows with the Windows SDK.

Options:
  -h, --help             Show help
  --version              Show version
  --format <human|json>  Select output format

result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic size [options]

Measure a published application and write a size report.

Options:
  --aot                           Publish with Native AOT, the default. [conflicts: no-aot]
  --no-aot                        Publish without Native AOT. [conflicts: aot]
  --verify-argument <verify-arguments...>
                                  An argument for the --verify executable. Repeat it for several
                                  arguments.
  --self-contained                Publish self-contained, the default.
                                  [conflicts: no-self-contained]
  --no-self-contained             Publish framework-dependent, with -p:SelfContained=false, for
                                  example to compare with a self-contained build. Combine it with
                                  --no-aot. [conflicts: self-contained]
  --property <NAME=VALUE...>      Pass an MSBuild property to the evaluation and publish, as dotnet
                                  publish -p does, for example OptimizationPreference=Speed. Repeat
                                  it for several properties. Configuration, RuntimeIdentifier,
                                  PublishAot and SelfContained have their own options.
  --project, -p <project>         The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                                  current directory.
  --runtime, --rid, -r <runtime>  The runtime identifier to publish for, for example linux-x64.
                                  Required.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                                  The build configuration. [default: Release]
  --report <report>               The JSON report to write. The file must not exist yet. Default:
                                  runic-size-<runtime>-<UTC time>.json in the current directory.
  --verify <verify>               An executable to run after a successful publish, as a path or a
                                  command on PATH, such as node. It receives the --verify-argument
    
[truncated]

                              default.
  --entry-point <path>        Entry document relative to the source directory. [default: index.html]

  --version                   Show version
  --format <human|json>       Select output format

Usage: dotnet runic package flathub [options]

Write a Flathub source-build manifest with offline NuGet and npm sources from the committed lock
files. --build builds it with flatpak-builder on Linux.

Options:
  --build                  Build the manifest as Flathub does: install the runtime and SDK
                           extensions, download the sources, then build offline and write a bundle.
                           Linux only.
  --git-url <URL>          The application's git repository, which Flathub checks out. [required]
  --project, -p <project>  The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                           current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                           The build configuration to evaluate. [default: Release]
  --output-directory, -o <output-directory>
                           The directory to write the package to. Defaults to
                           artifacts/package/<target> beside the project.
  --git-commit <SHA>       Build this commit. [conflicts: git-tag]
  --git-tag <TAG>          Build this tag. [conflicts: git-commit]
  -h, --help               Show help
  --version                Show version
  --format <human|json>    Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic package flathub --git-url https://github.com/example/notes.git --git-tag v1.2.0
  dotnet runic package flathub --git-url https://github.com/example/notes.git --git-commit 0123abcd 
--build

Package the application as an .app bundle in a disk image, and with --pkg an installer package. Runs

                                  requires, as RunicMacSandbox does: the sandbox, loopback network,
                                  user-selected files and bookmark entitlements.
  --pkg                           Also write an installer package with productbuild that installs
                                  the bundle in /Applications, as App Store Connect takes it.
  --project, -p <project>         The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                                  current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                                  The build configuration to publish. [default: Release]

                                  architecture on the target's operating system. Runic supports
                                  osx-arm64 (Apple silicon) only.
  --output-directory, -o <output-directory>
                                  The directory to write the package to. Defaults to
                                  artifacts/package/<target> beside the project.
  --sign <IDENTITY>               Sign with this identity from the keychain instead of ad hoc:
                                  Developer ID Application, or Apple Distribution for the Mac App
                                  Store.
  --notary-profile <NAME>         Notarize and staple the disk image, and a signed installer
                                  package, with this notarytool keychain profile. [requires: sign]
  --provisioning-profile <FILE>   Embed this provisioning profile as

Usage: dotnet runic package rpm [options]

Package the application as an rpm. Runs on Linux with rpmbuild, also on Debian and Ubuntu.

Options:
  --project, -p <project>         The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                                  current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                                  The build configuration to publish. [default: Release]
  --runtime, --rid, -r <runtime>  The runtime identifier to publish for. Defaults to the host's
                                  architecture on the target's operating system.
  --output-directory, -o <output-directory>
                                  The directory to write the package to. Defaults to
                                  artifacts/package/<target> beside the project.
  -h, --help                      Show help
  --version                       Show version
  --format <human|json>           Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic package rpm
  dotnet runic package rpm --runtime linux-arm64

result.stdout:
Usage: dotnet runic package windows [options]

Package the application as an MSIX package. Runs on Windows with the Windows SDK.

Options:
  --project, -p <project>         The project file, or a directory with one .csproj. Defaults to the
                                  current directory.
  --configuration, -c <configuration>
                                  The build configuration to publish. [default: Release]
  --runtime, --rid, -r <runtime>  The runtime identifier to publish for. Defaults to the host's
                                  architecture on the target's operating system.
  --output-directory, -o <output-directory>
                                  The directory to write the package to. Defaults to
                                  artifacts/package/<target> beside the project.
  --publisher <CN=...>            The package's Publisher, which must equal the signing
                                  certificate's subject. Defaults to RunicApplicationPublisher.
  --certificate <PFX>             Sign the package with this PFX file; its password comes from
                                  RUNIC_SIGNING_PASSWORD. [conflicts: thumbprint]
  --thumbprint <SHA1>             Sign the package with the certificate of this SHA-1 thumbprint
                                  from the certificate store. [conflicts: certificate]
  --timestamp-url <URL>           Timestamp the signature with this RFC 3161 server.
  -h, --help                      Show help
  --version                       Show version
  --format <human|json>           Select output format

Examples:
  dotnet runic package windows
  dotnet runic package windows --certificate app.pfx --timestamp-url http://timestamp.digicert.com
